title: Locomotion Dynamics of a Vibration-Driven Robot with Spring–Damper Coupling via Non-Newtonian Fluids
content: Vibration-driven robots represent a lightweight and mechanically simple class of locomo tion systems that achieve propulsion through oscillation-induced frictional interactions with the ground, eliminating the need for wheels, legs, or tracks. Despite their promise for tasks such as in-pipe inspection, debris clearance, and small-scale medical operations, most existing models assume purely elastic coupling or linear viscous damping, thereby 1 2 3 4 5 6 neglecting complex dissipative phenomena. This study introduces and analyzes a two- 7 module vibration-driven robot in which the interconnecting element is a spring–damper 8 system filled with a non-Newtonian fluid. The effective damping in this configuration 9 is nonlinear and explicitly dependent on the angular velocity of the unbalanced rotating 10 mass, resulting in strong coupling between actuator dynamics and energy dissipation. A 11 set of governing dynamic equations is derived to capture these interactions and is validated 12 through numerical simulation. Parametric studies are conducted to quantify the influence 13 of design variables such as mass, stiffness, and fluid rheological properties on locomotion 14 velocity and energetic cost. The results demonstrate that nonlinear damping introduced by 15 non-Newtonian fluids significantly alters locomotion regimes, enabling adaptive trade-offs 16 between stability, efficiency, and speed. These findings highlight the potential of velocity- 17 dependent damping to enhance vibration-driven locomotion and provide new pathways 18 for the design and control of next-generation energy-efficient mobile robots.
